title: Amazon White Background Photo Guide | AIVideosUGC
description: Make an Amazon white-background main image from a phone photo. Use pure white (RGB 255), fill 85% or more of the square, and add nothing extra.
h1: How to Make an Amazon White Background Photo for Your Main Image
lead: Shoppers meet your blender in a square that fills the frame. Put the blender you ship large on white, and keep the sale badge off this picture.
summary: A large product on white is what shoppers see first. The square stays white, the product stays large, and the frame stays limited to what the box contains.

sections.h2: What Amazon Asks of the Main Image
paras: Shoppers see the product you sell, on pure white, with nothing extra in the square. Sale stickers, badges, and extra objects stay off this picture.

Start with the corners. Amazon's image guide wants those corners at 255 on red, green, and blue. The product should take most of the square, and it should be the one you ship, in the form you pack it. Clothing and jewelry can add further rules, so read the current Seller Central page for your category before you upload. The longest side is usually at least 500 pixels, and 1000 pixels if you want the zoom. Stay under the maximum size they publish for that category.
sections.alt: Olive canvas backpack centered on a pure white background.

paras: A shop with thirty totes can reuse the white square for tote thirty. Save the setup once the first tote looks right.
A clean main image can also be the first picture on your own store.
You set pure white once, choose how much of the square the product fills, and name what ships in the box. The next product uses that setup.
You confirm shape, color, parts, and label against the product in your hand, and then you publish the file that matches.

sections.h2: Does the Phone Photo Need to Start on White
paras: No. It needs the whole product, sharp, with even light and a little space around every edge.

Take the photo near a window, on a plain surface, and hold the phone at the product's height. Show what the buyer finds in the box. When two lids ship with the bottle, both lids belong in the photo. When a strap is sold separately, the photo shows the item without that strap.
sections.alt: Adult hand holds an olive canvas backpack upright beside a bright window.

sections.h2: How to Make the Pure White Main Image
paras: The kettle and both lids are already in the phone photo, and that group is what you ask for on white.

Open the [AI product background changer](page:change-background) or the [AI product photo generator](page:photo-hub). Type one plain line, such as the kettle and both lids on white. Then look at a corner. A corner at 255 on red, green, and blue means it is ready.
sections.alt: Olive canvas backpack on a pure white background.

sections.h2: The Same White Setup Across the Catalog
paras: A white main image keeps a lamp listing easy to find in search. Replace a gray main image and the listing can show in search again. The later photos are not the ones this rule is about.
Once the first lamp's square is right, use that same square on the next lamp. An API can start the job from the catalog you already keep, so a new color uses the setup you already saved.

sections.h2: One Look Across the Later Images
paras: Save the shop's navy and the wordmark for the photos after the main image. Those later photos are where the brand kit's colors and wordmark belong. The main image stays a clean product on white.

The white square is only the first picture. A pan on a stove, or a hand on the handle for scale, belongs in the later spots. [Photos of daily use](page:lifestyle-photos) and [photos with a person](page:model-photos) are those spots. Put the brand kit on those later photos.

sections.h2: How to Make the Listing Photos in 3 Steps
paras: Get the main image right on one backpack before you touch the rest. The square is white, and the straps are in it when the straps ship.
The second picture can be the backpack on a chair, with your navy caption added in your own editor. Match the long side to the size your category currently asks for.
When that pair looks right, repeat it for the other backpacks and send the files to Seller Central. Upload the white file you already checked.
A two-person shop can give a cutting board a white main image with the product it already pays for. The white square is a job in that product.
The bill you already know is the plan and the credits. That is the whole bill, including a quiet month like July.
When the photo tools get better, that shows up in the product you already open, on the day you open it.
November is when thirty new colors show up at once. The white setup from October still applies, and an API can start those files from the catalog.
The navy on the later Amazon photo should be the navy on your own store. Set it once. The white main image stays free of lettering.

sections.h2: How a Catalog Seller Uses the Main Image
paras: Every new product gets the same pure-white main image. Photos of the product in daily use stay in the later image spots.

sections.h2: More Photo Tools for the Listing
paras: [Background changer](page:change-background) takes off the old background. [White background](page:white-background) is the tool for the main image. [Product photos](page:photo-hub) is the wider set of photo tools. [Photos of daily use](page:lifestyle-photos) fill the later spots.

sections.h2: What to Check Before You Upload
paras: You upload a file whose corners are full white and whose product matches the one in your hand. Check the corners with a color picker, then set the real product next to the screen and compare shape, color, parts, and label.

Each corner should be pure white, with no gray haze. Zoom in on labels, because small lettering is where a new image often goes wrong. If the words are wrong, try again from a sharper photo. Also check the longest side against Amazon's current size note for your category.
sections.alt: Adult hands compare an olive canvas backpack with a blank white square card.

sections.h2: What If the Product Is White, Clear, or a Set
paras: Set the item's shape first, light the edges, and show exactly how many pieces the listing sells.

Side light keeps a white product's outline visible on white. Take the starting photo with light from one side, so the outline has soft shading, and mention that side light in the line you type. Clear glass shows the room behind it, so photograph it away from busy clutter. When the listing sells a set, every piece that ships belongs in the main image.
sections.alt: Adult hand shapes an olive canvas backpack upright on a white sweep.

sections.h2: Should Every Listing Image Be White
paras: Only the first picture has to be the white square. Picture two can show the mug in a kitchen. Picture three can show the rim up close.

A useful set might show the sneaker in a gym bag, a hand for size, and a close view of the sole. Make the pictures first, then add any words in your own editor. A soft shadow, when you want one, belongs on a later image. See [Photos of daily use](page:lifestyle-photos).
sections.alt: Adult holds an olive canvas backpack in a simple product gallery setup.

paras: A large product, white corners, the right parts, and a readable label are the file you upload. Check the item in your hand against that file.

The phone photo can start on any plain surface. One finished image is 24 credits, shown before it starts. If it does not finish, those credits come back. The same white setup can repeat across the catalog, including through an API.

faq.q: What does Amazon want on the main image?
faq.a: The product you ship, large in the square, on white that reads 255 on red, green, and blue. A sticker, a badge, or an extra piece stays off the picture. Clothing and jewelry can add more rules, so read the current Seller Central note for your category before you upload.

faq.q: What happens if the main image breaks the rules?
faq.a: The listing can return to search once that main image is fixed. A kitchen photo belongs in a later slot. The main image is the one that has to be white.

faq.q: How do I get a pure white background from a phone photo?
faq.a: Start from a phone photo that already shows the whole item. Ask for white, then sample a corner. A corner at 255 on red, green, and blue is ready for Seller Central. Read the label at a zoom before you upload.

faq.q: Can I do this for many products together?
faq.a: Yes. After the first item is right, the next colors can use that same square. Each color keeps that crop.

faq.q: Can my shop system start the white image?
faq.a: Yes. If your shop system already lists every item, it can send the photo and ask for the white square. You still check one file from the batch against the item in your hand before the rest go up.

faq.q: Why does my white background look gray on Amazon?
faq.a: The corners are not full white. Check them with a color picker and ask for RGB 255, 255, 255 again. A gray haze is enough for the image to fail.

faq.q: Can an image made here be my Amazon main image?
faq.a: Yes, if it shows the real product, on pure white, with nothing extra drawn on. Compare it with the item in your hand before you upload.

faq.q: How many credits does one white image use?
faq.a: 24 credits. The cost shows before the job starts. If it does not finish, those credits come back.
It keeps the shape in the photo you uploaded. If a handle, a lid, or the label shifts, try again from a sharper photo of that side, and publish the shape you ship.

faq.q: What if the product is white or clear?
faq.a: Light it from the side so the edge still reads, and keep every piece that ships in the frame. A white item on white needs that edge or it vanishes.
